experiments.title: 1. OCR engine bake-off and the hybrid choice
experiments.purpose: Pick the OCR engine for the two drawings. Priorities: digit fidelity, line boxes, no invented text, Traditional Chinese with CAD variants, tiny coloured pipe labels, local runtime.
experiments.method: Ground truth: 115 strings (81 sys sheet, 34 raft sheet), 40 marked CRITICAL, read by eye from 3-4x zoomed crops. Sheet-wide fuzzy match: hit = at least 85 % of GT characters recovered; digit % = share of numbers in the GT string found intact. Position-restricted zone test on the raft pipe-label band (7 CRITICAL strings). Same page handling for every engine. PP-OCR: 1280 px tiles, 160 px overlap. VLMs: 640 px tiles, 120 px overlap, 2x zoom. Variants: unclip ratio 2.0 and 2.5, 2x upscaled tiles.

configuration: PP-OCRv6 medium with unclip 2.0 (the hybrid base).

experiments.environment: M1 (RTX 3060 12 GB, shared, with a few CPU cores). Timings from concurrent jobs on one GPU.
experiments.duration: Per-engine seconds for both sheets are in the table. Hybrid: raft sheet 858 s, sys sheet 187 s (hybrid.log, measured). PaddleOCR-VL sys sheet alone 2,209 s.

rows: Solid baseline, weaker than v6 on digits.

experiments.judgement: OCR is not the main answer bottleneck. In a check of 16 wrong answers (hand-graded run), the correct value was already in the OCR text for 11. The hybrid is the best measured balance on these two drawings, not a claim of universal superiority. The digit regression is unexplained.

findings: Five questions (Q040, Q041, Q043, Q136, Q157) were wrong across five retained-40 readers. Q042 was correct in the bf16 baseline; Q037 was correct in both Qwen3.5 runs. These failures implicated the fact layer; the later held-out paired test measured the merged fixes.

4B Thinking FP8 vLLM scored 33 / 0 / 7 vs bf16 transformers 33 / 1 / 6: tied on correct count on 40 questions, graded by one reviewer. On M1, FP8 vLLM measured 64 tokens/s alone, 125 with two and 182 with three concurrent requests; three workers achieved about 3.3x faster per-question wall throughput than serial bf16.
The Mac 4-bit readers scored 31 correct vs 33 for M1 FP8, two fewer on the same 40; different quantization and hardware make them only indicative proxies for the 3060 result.
The vLLM HTTP backend supports concurrency via --workers N and DOCSEARCH_WEB_WORKERS; each web worker loads its own retrieval models, requiring 3–5 GB per worker.
Answer check and one retry scored 31 / 0 / 9 vs 33 / 1 / 6 without it, and took 346 vs 195 s per question; keep it off.
More chunks did not help: top-30 gave 21 correct against 22 for top-12 on the same 38 (4B).
A larger reader alone did not clear the bar: 9B at top-12 gave +1 over 4B on 38 (23 against 22), below the +4 net needed to count as better.
Fact rows gave +6 for 4B on the development set (22 to 28 of 38; seven fixed, Q037 lost) and +4 for 9B (23 to 27 of 38). The fresh paired test decides whether they go on by default.
OCR is not the main bottleneck: in 16 wrong answers the correct value was already in the OCR text for 11.
Sampling noise is about 1 to 2 questions net (seed 1 vs seed 0).
Current 4B fact rows, retained 40: wrong Q037, Q040, Q041, Q043, Q136 and Q157; partial Q101.
Failure classes: near-identical tanks, wrong totals, counting, false NOT FOUND, OCR misread of the pump bore.
More chunks and a bigger reader did not help; the next steps target the failure classes themselves (answer check, crop re-read).
The row-selection fix gained two questions, Q113 and Q115.

The stricter component-based context judge supersedes the earlier Q045-uncovered finding: Q045 has both sum components in every index; the reader must add them. Final-v3, final-v3b, final-v4 and mac-trace2 each have 146 correct, 1 weak and 3 not checkable.
Held-out fixed versus baseline: 69 / 5 / 5 versus 67 / 4 / 8 on 79; the unseen 58 show no measurable gain outside Q136 and Q157, and the overlap is not independent evidence.
On 37 retained ids, hand grades are 35 / 0 / 2 for 4B, 30 / 4 / 3 for 2B thinking on, 30 / 3 / 4 for 0.8B thinking off, and 26 / 0 / 11 for 1.7B thinking on.
Mac pipeline timing: Thinking 4-bit with 3 workers took 1706 s for 12 ids; 4 workers provided no 4-bit speedup and caused errors with 8-bit and bf16.
Best Mac result and time: Qwen3-4B-Thinking 4-bit with 3 workers, 11 / 12 correct in 1706 s. Best 3060 accuracy: 4B FP8, 122 / 146 correct (84%).

Mac 150-question run, Qwen3.5-0.8B bf16 thinking off: 115 / 15 / 20 on 150 (77% correct) in 1019 s wall, 16 correct below Qwen3-4B-Thinking 4-bit (131) at about 17x less wall time, with no abstention on Q151 to Q153. Accuracy-first default stays Qwen3-4B-Thinking 4-bit; Qwen3.5-0.8B thinking off is the speed option.

caveats: Cross-machine and precision comparisons mix RTX 3060 FP8/AWQ and Mac 4-bit MLX hardware and quantization; seeds do not reproduce across engines.
Earlier hand grades were assigned by one reviewer without independent validation.

Per-question hand labels were reconstructed cell by cell on 2026-11-17; the recount differs from earlier totals by up to 3 correct per run because partial credit is now applied consistently. Benchmark v1.4 (2026-11-17) revised the wording or reference of Q036, Q043, Q044 and Q045 (ids only; text not recorded here).
The 40-question subset is small, overlaps with development, and was used while tuning prompts, chunking and calculator behaviour.
Differences below about 4 questions net are treated as noise.
Vendor and community numbers are not verified by this project.
Timings are from shared hardware (RTX 3060 shared; Mac mini shared, other services stopped 2026-11-16).
The tailnet web service has no login.
The automatic grader is conservative: it never passes a wrong answer and rejects some correct ones. Hand grades are the reference.
Same-machine repeat builds had identical chunk text (1120 of 1120); mac-trace2 and final-v3 had 924 of 1265 matching normalized chunk bodies despite identical source PDF md5 and cascade counts.
Context presence and loose numeric matching can accept wrong-label selections; long small-model outputs can be incorrectly failed by the first-sentence automatic grader.
Mac pipeline server reachability errors have an unknown cause; the 9-error timing cell is invalid.
The new graders are LLM sub-agents, not the human; 12 questions per Mac cell is a small sample.
The 3060 machine's Hugging Face cache was deleted on 2026-11-23; 3060 runs need re-downloads.
